purpose: Archived N=10 three-backend window on a low-end x86 host: eight capabilities measured with the Rust engine against Biopython- and Biostrings-based arms, plus a record-granularity experiment testing whether language-boundary crossings explain the sequence.stats parity. Also the first window in which the R backend executed as a real third arm.

methodology.warmup: one untimed warmup per backend before the timed repeats; the warmup is excluded from the report, which holds exactly 10 timed runs (run_index 1..10)
methodology.disclosure: Serial execution with no concurrent build, lint or archiving; CPU governor fixed at powersave for the whole window; inputs are staged on tmpfs so no disk latency enters the measurement; backend order fixed at rust->python->r, so cross-backend frequency/thermal drift is a known limitation. Ratios hold for this machine and these inputs only; per-run wall times are archived so they can be re-checked.

environment.cpu_model: Intel(R) Pentium(R) Gold G7400 (2 cores / 4 threads; cpufreq governor fixed at powersave for the whole window)
environment.gpu: not used by this benchmark; the host additionally carries a GTX 750 Ti and an integrated UHD 710 (both exercised only by the separate gpu-lab carrier, out of scope here)
environment.memory: 15756 MB usable host memory; resident per-phase peak recorded per run (VmHWM)
environment.storage: root on btrfs over a 512 GB NVMe (Netac); /tmp is tmpfs (7.7 GB) so every benchmark input is RAM-backed; two spinning disks (ST1000DM003, ST500DM002) present and unused by these runs

data_sources.note: random.seed(42); matrix.tsv (2000x40), sets.tsv (20k x 4 sets with repeated occupancy masks), structure.pdb (3000 residues / 24k atoms), variants.vcf (200k records), genes.txt + associations.tsv (5k genes / 45k annotations). Digests in inputs.sha256; byte-identical on Windows/Python 3.13 and Linux/Python 3.14.
big.fa via the engine simulator (--count 20 --length 5000000 --seed 42); reads200.fq via simulate reads on big.fa (--read-length 150 --coverage 100 --seed 42). Digests in inputs.sha256.
numpy default_rng(42); the same ~100 Mb of FASTA as 1x100 Mb, 20x5 Mb and 100k x 1 kb. Digests in inputs.sha256.

entries.dataset: 2000 x 40 count matrix (4 groups x 10 samples)
3000 residues / 24k atoms synthetic PDB with pLDDT column

side_experiments.note: Record-shape experiment (1 x 100 Mb / 20 x 5 Mb / 100k x 1 kb) run with the same capability but deliberately kept out of the entries above: three runs of sequence.stats.v1 in one summary would collide on the capability key. The reports are archived beside this summary as sequence.stats.v1.granularity-<shape>.benchmark.json for provenance, and the figures read them through --granularity.
